title: D3D12: GPU device removed (0x887a0005) on Intel Arc when rendering alpha-scissor materials — sensitive to how the mesh data reached the GPU
body:
### Tested versions

- Godot 4.7.stable.mono and 4.7.1.rc1.mono — reproducible in both
- Not reproducible with the Vulkan driver on the same machine/GPU
- Not reproducible with D3D12 on a non-Intel GPU (dev machine)

### System information

We encounter an issue me and my brother who trying to make a little game for fun.
But we encountered a lot of issues with intel. Here is what we found / did so far :

- Windows 11 Pro, Intel Arc Pro B50/B580 (Battlemage), driver: <ALL> - Forward+, D3D12, Shader Model 12_0 path - Reproducible in exported release builds, when running scenes from CLI, and in the editor 3D viewport

### Issue description

Rendering a few hundred instances of an **imported mesh with a discard-based material** (custom spatial shader with `ALPHA_SCISSOR_THRESHOLD`, foliage cutout) hangs the GPU within seconds. Windows removes the device; every subsequent call fails with `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`:

```
ERROR: Condition "!((HRESULT)(res) >= 0)" is true. Returning: ERR_UNAVAILABLE
   at: swap_chain_resize (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:2799)
ERROR: CreateResource failed with error 0x887a0005.
   at: (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:1404)
```

Raising `TdrDelay` barely helps, which suggests a GPU fault rather than a plain timeout.

The remarkable part: **the same triangles with the same material either crash or work depending on how the mesh data reached the GPU.** After ~30 bisection runs on the affected hardware:

| # | Configuration (300 instances unless noted) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ArrayMesh **deserialized from .tscn** + scissor shader | 💥 device removed |
| 2 | Same mesh re-encoded at runtime (`surface_get_arrays` → `add_surface_from_arrays`, no LODs) | ✅ stable |
| 3 | Same runtime re-encode + `ImporterMesh.generate_lods()` | 💥 |
| 4 | Same re-encode, then `PackedScene.pack()` + `instantiate()` | 💥 |
| 5 | Any of the above with the scissor removed (opaque leaves) | ✅ |
| 6 | Scissor swapped for `ALPHA_HASH` / manual `discard;` / without `cull_disabled` / shadows disabled / shadow_mesh stripped / LOD arrays stripped from the .tscn | 💥 (any discard form, config #1) |
| 7 | MultiMesh with the re-encoded mesh, 2 000 instances, shadows on | ✅ |
| 8 | Same as #7 + `visibility_range_end` 65 m and `visibility_range_fade_mode = SELF` (dither), camera in the fade band | 💥 |
| 9 | 20 000 procedural `PlaneMesh` quads with the same scissor shader (multimesh or 300 separate nodes) | ✅ |
| 10 | `Sprite3D`/`Label3D` with `shaded = true` + `alpha_cut = Discard` (non-billboard), first draw | 💥 (the Y-billboard variant of the same flags, used elsewhere, is fine) |

So the discard-family pipeline variants (depth prepass / shadow passes with alpha test?) fault only when fed by specific data paths: **deserialized surface buffers, runtime-generated mesh LODs, the visibility-range dither fade, and some sprite/label variants** — while runtime-built buffers without LODs render the identical content correctly.

Rows 2 vs 3 and 2 vs 4 are controlled pairs: a single `generate_lods()` call (or a `pack()` round-trip) is the only difference between stable and device-removed.

Additional observations:

- One or two instances are often fine; a few hundred crash within seconds (sometimes only when the instances enter the frustum).
- Shader baker on/off at export: no difference.
- `--gpu-validate`: no difference, and no debug-layer message precedes the removal.


### Steps to reproduce

Attached minimal project (no C#, ~30 MB with the tree asset). Each scene maps to a row above:

```
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor --import          # once
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor repro_trees.tscn        # row 1  -> device removed
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor repro_K_rebuilt.tscn    # row 2  -> stable
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor repro_K3_lods.tscn      # row 3  -> device removed
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor repro_D_opaque.tscn     # row 5  -> stable
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor repro_R2_fade.tscn      # row 8  -> device removed
godot --path repro_d3d12_scissor main_heavy.tscn         # row 9  -> stable
```

Opening `repro_trees.tscn` in the editor 3D viewport also kills the editor on affected hardware.

## Workarounds (verified in production)

Gated at runtime to `d3d12` + Intel adapter:

1. Re-encode foliage ArrayMeshes through `add_surface_from_arrays` into fresh mesh objects at scene-instantiation time (drops LODs). Do **not** re-pack the scene afterwards — packing brings the crash back (row 4).
2. Force `visibility_range_fade_mode = DISABLED` on instanced foliage.
3. Prefer MultiMesh over per-node scene duplicates for dense foliage.
4. Force `shaded = false` / `alpha_cut = Disabled` on Sprite3D/Label3D item drops.

## Attribution

Unclear whether the root cause is the D3D12 backend or the Intel driver. The fact that deserialized buffers and runtime-built buffers of the same surface behave differently suggests the backend uploads them differently (alignment/offsets/layout?), and the Intel driver is the only one that faults on the difference.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Here is the projet use for debugging this.
https://download.wagnardsoft.com/repro_d3d12_scissor.zip
